impacts.summary: Everything this printing plant reports goes into the air as ozone, about 46,600 lb in 2024.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.how: Ground-level ozone irritates the airways, causing coughing, a sore throat and chest tightness. Packaging printers usually make it with equipment that treats plastic film before printing. Ozone breaks down within hours, so the effect stays close to the plant.
avoid: Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days
Plan outdoor exercise for mornings, when ozone is lower
Report strong or unusual odors to the Wisconsin DNR

impacts.title: Kids & people with asthma
impacts.where: Family Services of Northeast Wisconsin is within 1 mile
impacts.how: Children, older adults and anyone with asthma feel ozone first, and it can trigger asthma attacks.
avoid: Keep rescue inhalers handy on high-ozone days
Move kids' outdoor play indoors when the air quality index is orange or worse
Ask the DNR whether the plant's ozone is covered by an air permit

impacts.summary: Almost all of this mill's releases go straight into the Fox River, about 2 miles above where it meets the bay.

impacts.title: Fish & river life
impacts.how: About 230,000 lb of nitrates and 150 lb of ammonia reached the river in 2024. Extra nutrients feed algae that use up the oxygen fish need to breathe, and ammonia is directly toxic to fish at high levels. The mill also released 57 lb of lead, which settles into river mud and builds up in fish over time.
avoid: Follow the Wisconsin DNR fish advisory for the Fox River before eating your catch
Keep smaller, younger fish, and trim skin and fat, where pollutants collect
Use less lawn fertilizer: runoff adds even more nutrients to the same river

impacts.title: Swimming & beaches
impacts.how: The Fox River carries these nutrients into the bay, where they can help fuel algae blooms that close beaches and turn the water green. The Fox is already listed as impaired for nutrients; this mill is one possible contributor.
avoid: Check beach advisories before swimming
Stay out of water that looks green, scummy or smells bad, and keep pets out too
Rinse off after swimming in the bay

impacts.title: Air in the neighborhood
impacts.how: About 14,700 lb of methanol and 3,900 lb of ammonia went into the air in 2024. Methanol can cause headaches and dizziness at high levels, and ammonia irritates the eyes, nose and throat.
avoid: Check the daily air quality index (AirNow) on hot, still days
Report strong or unusual odors to the Wisconsin DNR
Keep windows closed when odors are noticeable

impacts.title: Birds & wildlife
impacts.where: Fox River and Green Bay shoreline
impacts.how: Lead and mercury don't break down. They build up in fish, then in the eagles, cormorants and gulls that eat them, and can harm their nerves and breeding.
avoid: Use lead-free fishing tackle so less lead ends up in the river
Support shoreline habitat restoration along the lower Fox
Report sick or dead birds to the Wisconsin DNR

impacts.summary: This plant coats labels and paper. It released about 24,000 lb of vinyl acetate into the air in 2024.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.how: Vinyl acetate is a vapor from the adhesives and coatings used here. It irritates the eyes, nose and throat.
avoid: Report strong or unusual odors to the Wisconsin DNR
Keep windows closed when the smell is noticeable
Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days

impacts.title: Long-term health
impacts.how: The International Agency for Research on Cancer lists vinyl acetate as possibly carcinogenic to humans. The risk depends on how much people breathe in over many years.
avoid: Look up the plant's yearly releases in EPA's Toxics Release Inventory
Comment on the plant's air permit when the DNR opens it for public input
Ask the plant about plans to cut vapor emissions

impacts.summary: This aluminum foundry released about 3,700 lb to the air in 2024, mostly the solvent tetrachloroethylene.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.where: North side of Manitowoc, within 1 mile: 3,747 residents
impacts.how: About 2,600 lb of tetrachloroethylene, which EPA lists as likely to cause cancer, went into the air, plus 500 lb of formaldehyde and small amounts of nickel. Both solvents irritate the eyes and lungs.
avoid: Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days
Report strong or unusual odors to the Wisconsin DNR
Comment on the plant's air permit when the DNR opens it for public input

impacts.title: Seniors & schools
impacts.where: 23% of nearby residents are seniors; 4 schools within 1 mile
impacts.how: This neighborhood has Manitowoc's highest share of older residents, who are more sensitive to air pollution, along with four schools.
avoid: Older adults with heart or lung disease should limit time outdoors on poor-air days
Ask schools whether they track the air quality index
Join DNR public hearings, like the one held in 2023 on the foundry's new furnaces

impacts.title: Groundwater
impacts.how: Tetrachloroethylene lasts a long time in groundwater wherever it reaches the soil. It's released here to the air, so this is a possible pathway rather than a confirmed one.
avoid: If you use a private well, test it for volatile organic compounds (VOCs)
City water users are on Lake Michigan water
Report spills or strong solvent smells to the DNR

impacts.summary: This metal-plating shop released about 5,500 lb to the air in 2024, almost all zinc, and sent more to the city sewer plant.

impacts.title: Air & dust
impacts.how: About 5,500 lb of zinc compounds went into the air as fine dust and fumes, which settle nearby. Breathing zinc fumes can cause flu-like symptoms. Small amounts of nickel, a carcinogen, and chromium were also released.
avoid: Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days
Wipe dusty windowsills with a damp cloth instead of sweeping
Report strong or unusual odors to the Wisconsin DNR

impacts.title: Sewer & Lake Michigan
impacts.where: Manitowoc's wastewater plant, then Lake Michigan
impacts.how: The shop sent about 1,600 lb of nitrates plus some zinc and chromium down the sewer. The city's treatment plant removes much of this before its water reaches Lake Michigan. The exact route still needs to be confirmed.
avoid: Never pour chemicals, paint or oil down drains
Check DNR Beach Health before swimming at Manitowoc beaches
Follow the Lake Michigan fish advisory before eating your catch

impacts.title: Soil & yards
impacts.where: Homes and schoolyards near the shop
impacts.how: Metal dust that settles builds up in soil over time, where kids can swallow it while playing.
avoid: Wash kids' hands after outdoor play
Test garden soil before growing food
Take shoes off at the door

impacts.summary: Manitowoc's city-owned power plant released about 9,200 lb to the air in 2024, mostly hydrochloric acid from burning fuel.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.how: About 7,200 lb of hydrochloric acid and 2,000 lb of ammonia went into the air. Both irritate the eyes, nose and lungs. The plant mostly burns wood now, with some petroleum coke and coal, and it is switching two boilers to renewable fuel pellets.
avoid: Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days
Keep kids with asthma indoors when the air quality index is orange or worse
Follow MPU's switch to cleaner fuel at city utility meetings

impacts.title: Soil & gardens
impacts.where: Yards and gardens near the plant
impacts.how: The plant also released 3 lb of lead compounds. Lead doesn't break down: it settles onto soil and stays there, and small children are the most at risk.
avoid: Test garden soil for lead before growing food near the plant
Wash vegetables and hands after gardening
Take shoes off at the door so soil dust stays outside

impacts.summary: Sheboygan's largest air releaser: this coal plant on the lakeshore released about 61,700 lb in 2024. It plans to switch to natural gas in 2028.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.how: About 35,200 lb of ammonia and 25,200 lb of hydrogen fluoride, an acid gas from burning coal, went into the air. Both strongly irritate the eyes, nose and lungs.
avoid: Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days
Keep kids with asthma indoors when the air quality index is orange or worse
Follow the plant's coal-to-gas conversion and comment when it comes up for review

impacts.title: Lake Michigan fish
impacts.how: The plant released 6.3 lb of mercury and 45 lb of lead. Both settle onto the lake and build up in fish. Lake Michigan's mercury advisory comes mostly from regional and global sources, so this plant is one possible contributor.
avoid: Follow the Lake Michigan fish advisory (DNR Choose Wisely) before eating your catch
Keep smaller, younger fish
Pregnant people and kids should be extra careful with fish meals

impacts.title: Smog
impacts.how: Burning coal gives off nitrogen oxides, which form ground-level ozone (smog) on sunny days. Lakeshore Sheboygan County doesn't meet the federal ozone standard. Much of that ozone also blows in from Chicago and Milwaukee.
avoid: Plan outdoor exercise for mornings on hot, sunny days
Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days
Drive less on ozone action days

impacts.title: Lake water & beaches
impacts.where: Lake Michigan shoreline by the plant
impacts.how: The plant's water permit was out of compliance in 10 of the last 12 quarters. Most of that was late reports, but its discharge broke the pH limit three times and the solids limit once. Small amounts of barium, lead and vanadium also reached the lake.
avoid: Check DNR Beach Health before swimming
Rinse off after swimming
Report discolored water near the plant to the DNR

impacts.summary: This resin plant released about 28,600 lb to the air in 2024, mostly methanol and formaldehyde, and sent more to the city sewer plant.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.where: Within 1 mile: 8,731 residents, 660 children under 5, 6 schools
impacts.how: About 6,400 lb of formaldehyde, a known human carcinogen, went into the air, most of it escaping from leaks and vents rather than the smokestack. Another 19,600 lb of methanol was released. Both irritate the eyes, nose and throat.
avoid: Report strong or unusual odors to the Wisconsin DNR
Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days
Comment on the plant's air permit when the DNR opens it for public input

impacts.title: Smog
impacts.how: Methanol and formaldehyde help form ground-level ozone. Sheboygan's lakeshore doesn't meet the federal ozone standard, so this plant is one possible contributor.
avoid: Plan outdoor exercise for mornings on hot, sunny days
Keep rescue inhalers handy on high-ozone days
Drive less on ozone action days

impacts.title: Sewer & Lake Michigan
impacts.where: Sheboygan Regional Wastewater Treatment Facility, then Lake Michigan
impacts.how: The plant sent about 22,100 lb of formaldehyde, 10,700 lb of methanol and 2,200 lb of phenol to the sewer. These break down readily at the treatment plant before its water reaches Lake Michigan. The exact route still needs to be confirmed.
avoid: Never pour chemicals down drains
Check DNR Beach Health before swimming
Support upgrades at the regional wastewater plant

impacts.summary: This polymer plant released about 13,600 lb to the air in 2024, almost all methanol, plus a small amount to water.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.where: Within 1 mile: 3,952 residents; Horace Mann Middle School
impacts.how: About 13,600 lb of methanol went out the stack. At high levels methanol can cause headaches and dizziness. Small amounts of maleic anhydride, which can sensitize the lungs, were also released.
avoid: Report strong or unusual odors to the Wisconsin DNR
Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days
Ask the DNR whether the plant's methanol is covered by an air permit

impacts.title: Smog
impacts.how: Methanol helps form ground-level ozone, and Sheboygan's lakeshore doesn't meet the federal ozone standard.
avoid: Plan outdoor exercise for mornings on hot, sunny days
Drive less on ozone action days
Keep rescue inhalers handy on high-ozone days

impacts.title: Sheboygan River
impacts.how: About 15 lb of antimony and zinc reached water. That's small, and these aren't the river's main problem: older PCB pollution is why the DNR still says not to eat resident fish from the lower 14 miles of the river.
avoid: Don't eat resident fish from the lower 14 miles of the Sheboygan River
Follow the DNR fish advisory for other catches
Keep stormwater drains clear of trash and chemicals
